text:
marta: quick dump — ran an experimental bring-up for draft-quant-13b (4-bit per-channel, dynamic range) with speculative decoding toggled on for a small canary. posting high-level takeaways and config below, would love quick sanity checks :wave:

jed: nice — can you share the p50/p95 token latency and any delta on our QA benchmark? also what speculative strategy did you use (beam / sampling / early-exit)?

marta: sure. measured on our canary traffic (mix of chat + qa prompts, ~2k requests):
- baseline (no spec, same quant): p50 token latency 12ms -> with spec 7ms (approx 1.7x speedup), p95 220ms -> 120ms
- throughput (tokens/sec per GPU) improved ~1.8x for short (<=128) sequences
- quality: QA exact-match drop 0.6pp, answer-level BLEU down ~0.8; generative perplexity unchanged within noise
- failure mode: ~1.2% of requests hit fallback (we detect mismatch and rerun full decode)

sam: what was the detection check? how aggressive is the early mismatch heuristic?

marta: used conservative check_every=1 with beam=2 speculative sampling + greedy fallback. heuristic: compare top-1 token from spec path vs model path prefix logits; if mismatch in top-k (k=3) for 2 consecutive tokens, trigger fallback. in practice that keeps false positives low but still catches early drift.

kai: did you see quantization-related biases? 4-bit often shifts logits scale per-layer and can amplify spec drift. any per-layer clipping or outlier handling enabled?

marta: good call — we saw a consistent small logit shift in the last feedforward block for some prompts. fixed-by-experiment: per-channel scaling update on outlier rows reduced mismatch rate ~20%. ablation: when we disabled speculative on the last 2 layers, quality regressions vanished but performance hit partially reduced.

sam: config artifact pls?

marta: pasted the minimal config we used here:

```yaml
speculative:
  enabled: true
  strategy: beam
  beam_size: 2
  check_every: 1
  topk_check: 3
  fallback: full_decode
quant:
  type: per-channel-4bit
  outlier_clip: 0.999
  dynamic_scale: true
```

jed: did you run holdouts vs our core eval set (the 5k QA holdout)?

marta: yes — run id: http://internal/runs/613 (summary attached in the run). CI quick stats: overall QA EM 89.4% -> 88.8% (spec on), with fallback enabled the effective visible drop at endpoint is ~0.2pp because many failures roll back to full decode. we still need to think about tail cases: safety prompts and math chains are more sensitive.

kai: any tests on chain-of-thought (longer context)? speculative tends to break when conditioning is long.

marta: limited test: for sequences >512 tokens, spec benefits diminish and fallback increases to ~6%. recommend disabling spec by default for long-context routes until we improve prefix alignment heuristics.

sam: ops question — what do we need to ship a controlled canary? SLA-wise, p95 reduced so that's positive, but are we tracking token-level cost vs quality tradeoffs in Redwood Console?

marta: yes, hooked canary to console: cost/token saved ~28% for short queries but monitor alerts for EM drop >0.5pp. created a canary route `spec-13b-canary` with 5% traffic.

deploy-bot: canary deploy for `spec-13b-canary` finished: 12/12 checks passed, regression alarm threshold set to 0.5pp. :white_check_mark:

jed: next steps I suggest:
- run focused stress on safety/math prompts with spec off/on and last-layer-disabled variant
- try stronger outlier clipping and a per-layer scale recalibration during quantization
- capture logits snapshots for mismatch cases to train a better mismatch classifier (maybe a tiny binary NN)

marta: +1. I'll queue up the stress runs and push a follow-up with logs and a small pickle of logits for top mismatches. cc @sam for rollout plan.

sam: thanks — nice crisp experiment. keep it lightweight and let's avoid flipping spec on for high-risk routes until we have longer-run evals. :thumbsup:
